related_work_summary.title: Continuous Mott transition in semiconductor moire superlattices
related_work_summary.authors: T. Li, S. Jiang, L. Li, Y. Zhang, K. Kang, et al.
related_work_summary.relevance: Foundational experimental work on MoTe2/WSe2 moire system showing Mott transition and continuous tuning of interaction strength. Directly studies the same physical system as our benchmark paper (2111.01152).
key_contributions: Experimental demonstration of continuous Mott transition in MoTe2/WSe2
Electric tuning of effective interaction strength U/W
Scaling behavior of resistance near quantum critical point
related_work_summary.method_impact: Validates the physical relevance of the Hartree-Fock calculations being evaluated - the system has rich experimental phenomenology requiring theoretical HF treatment.

related_work_summary.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners (GPT-3)
related_work_summary.authors: T. Brown, B. Mann, N. Ryder, et al.
related_work_summary.relevance: Foundational work establishing LLM capability for task-agnostic reasoning. Demonstrates scaling laws for few-shot learning that underlie the expectation that LLMs can perform domain-specific reasoning.
related_work_summary.method_impact: Provides the theoretical foundation for expecting LLMs to perform complex physics calculations when given structured prompts. The structured template approach extends few-shot learning to multi-step scientific reasoning.

related_work_summary.title: Solving Quantitative Reasoning Problems with Language Models (Minerva)
related_work_summary.authors: A. Lewkowycz, A. Andreassen, D. Dohan, et al.
related_work_summary.relevance: Direct predecessor evaluating LLM quantitative reasoning on physics problems. Shows LLMs can solve ~30% of undergraduate physics problems correctly.
key_contributions: LLM achieves ~30% on undergraduate STEM problems
Training on technical content improves quantitative reasoning
related_work_summary.method_impact: Our benchmark extends Minerva's approach from undergraduate problem-solving to research-level multi-step derivations, using structured templates instead of chain-of-thought.

related_work_summary.title: Galactica: A Large Language Model for Science
related_work_summary.authors: R. Taylor, M. Kardas, G. Cucurull, et al.
related_work_summary.relevance: Demonstrates that LLMs trained on scientific corpora can store and reason about scientific knowledge. Outperforms GPT-3 on LaTeX equations (68.2% vs 49.0%).
key_contributions: Scientific corpus training improves domain performance
Strong performance on LaTeX equations and scientific reasoning
related_work_summary.method_impact: Suggests that LLMs with scientific pre-training could potentially improve the paper extraction step (in-paper content scoring), which is currently the weakest dimension in our benchmark.

cross_paper_insights: The MoTe2/WSe2 system has strong experimental motivation requiring accurate theoretical modeling
LLM quantitative reasoning has been demonstrated at undergraduate but not research level
Scientific corpus pre-training may improve domain-specific accuracy
Structured interfaces (templates, task tokens) are critical for scientific applications
